entries.title: Luke 23:1
segments: Then they all rose in a body and led Jesus before Pilate.

entries.title: Luke 23:2
segments: And they began to accuse him: "This is a man whom we found misleading our people, preventing them from paying taxes to the Emperor, and giving out that he himself is 'Christ, a King.'"

entries.title: Luke 23:3
segments: "Are you the King of the Jews?" Pilate asked him. "It is true," replied Jesus.

entries.title: Luke 23:4
segments: But Pilate, turning to the Chief Priests and the people, said: "I do not see anything to find fault with in this man."

entries.title: Luke 23:5
segments: But they insisted: "He is stirring up the people by his teaching all through Judea; he began with Galilee and has now come here."

entries.title: Luke 23:6
segments: Hearing this, Pilate asked if the man was a Galilean;

entries.title: Luke 23:7
segments: And, having satisfied himself that Jesus came under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who also was at Jerusalem at the time.

entries.title: Luke 23:8
segments: When Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly pleased, for he had been wanting to see him for a long time, having heard a great deal about him; and he was hoping to see some sign given by him.

entries.title: Luke 23:9
segments: So he questioned him at some length, but Jesus made no reply.

entries.title: Luke 23:10
segments: Meanwhile the Chief Priests and the Teachers of the Law stood by and vehemently accused him.

entries.title: Luke 23:11
segments: And Herod, with his soldiers, treated Jesus with scorn; he mocked him by throwing a gorgeous robe round him, and then sent him back to Pilate.

entries.title: Luke 23:12
segments: And Herod and Pilate became friends that very day, for before that there had been ill-will between them.

entries.title: Luke 23:13
segments: So Pilate summoned the Chief Priests, and the leading men, and the people,

entries.title: Luke 23:14
segments: And said to them: "You brought this man before me charged with misleading the people; and yet, for my part, though I examined him before you, I did not find this man to blame for any of the things of which you accuse him;

entries.title: Luke 23:15
segments: Nor did Herod either; for he has sent him back to us. And, as a fact, he has not done anything deserving death;

entries.title: Luke 23:16
segments: So I shall have him scourged, and then release him."

entries.title: Luke 23:17
segments: (Translation omits this verse)

entries.title: Luke 23:18
segments: But they began to shout as one man: "Kill this fellow, but release Barabbas for us."

entries.title: Luke 23:19
segments: (Barabbas was a man who had been put in prison for a riot that had broken out in the city and for murder.)

entries.title: Luke 23:20
segments: Pilate, however, wanting to release Jesus, called to them again;

entries.title: Luke 23:21
segments: But they kept calling out: "Crucify, crucify him!"

entries.title: Luke 23:22
segments: "Why, what harm has this man done?" Pilate said to them for the third time. "I have found nothing in him for which he could be condemned to death. So I will have him scourged, and then release him."

entries.title: Luke 23:23
segments: But they persisted in loudly demanding his crucifixion; and their clamor gained the day.

entries.title: Luke 23:24
segments: Pilate decided that their demand should be granted.

entries.title: Luke 23:25
segments: He released the man who had been put in prison for riot and murder, as they demanded, and gave Jesus up to be dealt with as they pleased.

entries.title: Luke 23:26
segments: And, as they were leading Jesus away, they laid hold of Simon from Cyrene, who was on his way in from the country, and they put the cross on his shoulders, for him to carry it behind Jesus.

entries.title: Luke 23:27
segments: There was a great crowd of people following him, many being women who were beating their breasts and wailing for him.

entries.title: Luke 23:28
segments: So Jesus turned and said to them: "Women of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.

entries.title: Luke 23:29
segments: A time, I tell you, is coming, when it will be said--'Happy are the women who are barren, and those who have never borne children or nursed them!'

entries.title: Luke 23:30
segments: At that time people will begin to say to the mountains 'Fall on us,' and to the hills 'Cover us.'

entries.title: Luke 23:31
segments: If what you see is done while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?"

entries.title: Luke 23:32
segments: There were two others also, criminals, led out to be executed with Jesus.

entries.title: Luke 23:33
segments: When they had reached the place called 'The Skull,' there they crucified Jesus and the criminals, one on the right, and one on the left.

entries.title: Luke 23:34
segments: [Then Jesus said: "Father, forgive them; they do not know what they are doing."] His clothes they divided among them by casting lots.

entries.title: Luke 23:35
segments: Meanwhile the people stood looking on. Even the leading men said with a sneer: "He saved others, let him save himself, if he is God's Christ, his Chosen One."

entries.title: Luke 23:36
segments: The soldiers, too, came up in mockery, bringing him common wine,

entries.title: Luke 23:37
segments: And saying as they did so: "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself."

entries.title: Luke 23:38
segments: Above him were the words--'THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.'

entries.title: Luke 23:39
segments: One of the criminals who were hanging beside Jesus railed at him. "Are not you the Christ? Save yourself and us," he said.

entries.title: Luke 23:40
segments: But the other rebuked him. "Have not you," he said, "any fear of God, now that you are under the same sentence?

entries.title: Luke 23:41
segments: And we justly so, for we are only reaping our deserts, but this man has not done anything wrong.

entries.title: Luke 23:42
segments: Jesus," he went on, "do not forget me when you have come to your Kingdom."

entries.title: Luke 23:43
segments: And Jesus answered: "I tell you, this very day you shall be with me in Paradise."

entries.title: Luke 23:44
segments: It was nearly mid-day, when a darkness came over the whole country, lasting till three in the afternoon,

entries.title: Luke 23:45
segments: The sun being eclipsed; and the Temple curtain was torn down the middle.

entries.title: Luke 23:46
segments: Then Jesus, with a loud cry, said: "Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit." And with these words he expired.

entries.title: Luke 23:47
segments: The Roman Captain, on seeing what had happened, praised God, exclaiming: "This must have been a good man!"

entries.title: Luke 23:48
segments: All the people who had collected to see the sight watched what occurred, and then went home beating their breasts.

entries.title: Luke 23:49
segments: All the friends of Jesus had been standing at a distance, with the women who accompanied him from Galilee, watching all this.

entries.title: Luke 23:50
segments: Now there was a man of the name of Joseph, who was a member of the Council, and who bore a good and upright character.

entries.title: Luke 23:51
segments: (This man had not assented to the decision and action of the Council.) He belonged to Ramah, a town in Judea, and lived in expectation of the Kingdom of God.

entries.title: Luke 23:52
segments: He now went to see Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus;

entries.title: Luke 23:53
segments: And, when he had taken it down, he wrapped it in a linen sheet, and laid him in a tomb cut out of stone, in which no one had yet been buried.

entries.title: Luke 23:54
segments: It was the Preparation Day, and just before the Sabbath began.

entries.title: Luke 23:55
segments: The women who had accompanied Jesus from Galilee followed, and saw the tomb and how the body of Jesus was laid,

entries.title: Luke 23:56
segments: And then went home, and prepared spices and perfumes. During the Sabbath they rested, as directed by the commandment
